articles.title: Meghan Markle's father found fit to face charges related to child sexual abuse images
articles.summary: An expert has determined that the 82-year-old estranged father of Meghan, the Duchess of Sussex, is mentally competent to face charges of keeping child sexual abuse material in storage in California,…

image.caption: Thomas Markle, the estranged father of Meghan Markle, has been found fit to face charges related to the storage of child sexual abuse materials in the United States. (Pinellas County Sheriff's Office/Handout/Reuters)

blocks.text: World

An expert has determined that the 82-year-old estranged father of Meghan, the Duchess of Sussex, is mentally competent to face charges of keeping child sexual abuse material in storage in California, a judge said Thursday.
Thomas Markle is being held in a Florida jail after allegedly cutting off his ankle monitor
Thomas Markle's defence lawyer said they would not contest the finding by Dr. Amie Gerodimos. The exam was ordered after his arrest at a senior care centre in Lakeland, Fla., on Nov. 6.
During a 90-minute interview, Markle denied the allegations against him and blamed his son for his legal troubles, according to Gerodimos's 15-page report.
"Why I am here. What have I done?" she quoted him as saying. "I don't have any child porn. I have no pictures of naked kids."

The FBI, however, said 78 items were seized from two storage units rented for years by Markle in the Los Angeles area, including slides, film negatives and books that contained suspected child sexual abuse images.
Some images appear to depict him with children, the FBI said.
Markle is in custody in a jail while the case remains in federal court in Tampa. It will eventually shift to a similar court in Southern California.
Security personnel outside the Lakeland, Fla., assisted living facility where Markle was arrested earlier this month. (Chris Urso/Reuters)
Markle was initially released on bond but was arrested again when authorities accused him of cutting off his electronic ankle monitor on Nov. 10.
He had a stroke earlier this year while living in the Philippines and had to have his left leg amputated. That forced him to return to the U.S. and settle in Florida.

The Sun, a British tabloid newspaper, reported that Meghan's half brother found child sexual abuse images while clearing out their father's home in the Philippines. The discovery led to a search of the two U.S. storage units in California, which Markle had rented since 2008.
"My son hates me. He has never accomplished anything," Markle told the psychiatrist.

Gerodimos said in her report that Markle, who has a number of health problems, understands the charges against him and can assist his lawyer — two key points in any competency determination. The expert said he was "malingering" at times during the interview.
Meghan Markle's father arrested, charged over child sexual abuse images
Investigation in the Philippines
Meanwhile, in the Philippines, Markle is under investigation for possession and intent to distribute images.

The Women and Children Protection Center, a branch of the Philippine National Police, filed a formal criminal complaint against Markle on Monday, police spokesperson Brig.-Gen. Allen Rae Co said in a written statement.

The complaint was filed with the prosecutor's office following an investigation into digital devices found at Markle's former home in Cebu City, the statement said. The prosecutor's office will assess the case for possible charges.
Markle mentioned the Philippines in his interview with Gerodimos, insisting "there's nothing incriminating" there.

Markle did not attend his daughter Meghan's 2018 wedding to Prince Harry at Windsor Castle. She said at the time he needed to tend to his health. Meghan is an American citizen who starred in the U.S. television drama Suits.

articles.title: This Sask. woman took some birds to a poultry show. Now avian flu is taking her whole flock
articles.summary: More than 18 million birds in Canada, including more than 1.2 million in Saskatchewan, have been lost due to the highly pathogenic disease since 2021.

image.caption: Christina Meyer with Huey, one of her geese that died from avian flu after she attended the Canadian National Poultry Show. (Christina Meyer/Facebook)

blocks.text: Saskatchewan
More than 18 million birds in Canada, including more than 1.2 million in Saskatchewan, have been lost due to the highly pathogenic disease since 2021.
CFIA confirms 11 infected flocks connected to national bird show, up from 3 on weekend
Christina Meyer didn't think her birds would win the show.
Still, she gave the chickens a bath to get ready. One of her geese, Frank, even won a second place ribbon.
But after she got home, three geese died from avian flu. Now she's waiting for the rest of the flock of over 100 birds to die or be culled.
"I feel sick to my stomach day and night, knowing what's going to happen. I haven't been able to really sleep. I haven't eaten well," said Meyer, who lives in the Saskatoon area.
Now she wants to spread awareness about the disease.
One of Christina Meyer's chickens taking a bath to prepare for the Canadian National Poultry Show on Nov. 7. (Our latest hobby farm/Facebook)
"I knew that if you have it, it's everybody. What I didn't know was how drastic and quickly it can hit," she said.
Meyer attended the Canadian National Poultry Show held on Nov. 7 in Moose Jaw through the Saskatchewan Poultry Association, which was the site of an avian flu outbreak.
The Canadian Food Inspection Agency (CFIA) has confirmed 11 cases of highly pathogenic avian flu connected to the show, up from three on Saturday.

items: Avian flu outbreak at national poultry show spreads to other provinces: CFIA

blocks.text: This includes five in Saskatchewan, four in Alberta and two in Manitoba, all in non-commercial flocks.
In Saskatchewan there have been two other recent detections in non-commercial flocks not related to the show, according to the CFIA.

items: B.C. watching closely after Washington state death linked to avian flu in dairy industry

blocks.text: Meyer said some breeders have lost years of progress.
"Because it's nationals, it has a bigger draw of people from further away bringing their best birds…. all those genetics and all those bloodlines are gone," she said.
The impact has also been emotional.
"Huey was one that died. He was really special too. He would give me hugs, kind of. He would eat grass out of my hand," she said.
Avian flu ongoing risk, says expert
Stephanie Smith, Saskatchewan's chief veterinary officer, said this is the first time she's heard of avian flu outbreak at a bird show.
"The fact that this was a show where people came from across provinces increases that concern, just because now we have potentially moved the virus many directions," Smith said.
Breeders can decide the risk level they want to take with their birds, and some steps could make shows safer, such as not holding them in the fall or spring, when transmission is higher, she said.
The general approach is to cull flocks in which there have been infections, Smith said.
Birds exposed to avian flu at national poultry show

"At this point if it's in a domestic flock the approach is to cull anything on site that could have been exposed, to try and keep that virus contained and then get it out of the environment as quickly as possible so we're not causing further spread."
Smith said properly cooking poultry and eggs ensures they're still safe to eat.
More than 18 million birds in Canada, including more than 1.2 million in Saskatchewan, have been lost due to highly pathogenic avian flu since 2021.
A notice issued by the federal government says the risk of avian influenza infection to most people in Canada "remains low."
ABOUT THE AUTHOR

Maeve Ellis is a reporter and associate producer with CBC News based in Saskatoon. You can reach her at maeve.ellis@cbc.ca or maeveellis_ on X. She would love to hear from anyone with Sask-related story ideas.

articles.title: Thomas Markle, Meghan’s father, is competent to face child sex abuse images case
articles.summary:
Judge in Florida says an expert has determined the 82-year-old estranged father of the Duchess of Sussex is mentally competent to face charges

An expert has determined that Thomas Markle,…

blocks.text: An expert has determined that Thomas Markle, the 82-year-old estranged father of the Duchess of Sussex, is mentally competent to face charges of keeping child sexual abuse material in storage in California, a judge said Thursday.
Markle’s defense lawyer said they would not contest the finding by Dr Amie Gerodimos. The exam was ordered after his arrest at a senior care center in Lakeland, Florida, on 6 November.

Investigators seized approximately 78 items from two storage units rented by Markle in the Los Angeles area, including slides, film negatives and books that contained suspected child sexual abuse images, according to the FBI.
Some images appear to depict him with children, the FBI said.
Markle is in custody while the case remains in federal court in Tampa. It will eventually shift to a similar court in southern California.
Markle was initially released on bond but was arrested again when authorities accused him of cutting off his electronic ankle monitor on 10 November.
He had a stroke earlier this year while living in the Philippines and had to have his left leg amputated. That forced him to return to the US and settle in Florida.

The Sun, a British tabloid newspaper, reported that Meghan’s half-brother found child sexual abuse images while clearing out their father’s home in the Philippines. The discovery led to a search of the two US storage units in California, which Markle had rented since 2008.

Meanwhile, in the Philippines, Markle is under investigation for possession and intent to distribute images. The Women and Children Protection Center, a branch of the Philippine National Police, filed a formal criminal complaint against Markle on Monday, police spokesperson Brig Gen Allen Rae Co said in a written statement.

The complaint was filed with the prosecutor’s office following an investigation into digital devices found at Markle’s former home in Cebu City, the statement said. The prosecutor’s office will assess the case for possible charges.

Markle did not attend his daughter Meghan’s 2018 wedding to Prince Harry at Windsor Castle. She said at the time he needed to tend to his health. Meghan is an American citizen who starred in the US television drama Suits.

articles.title: Tumbler Ridge shooter used ChatGPT to build 3D gun parts, U.S. magazine reports
articles.summary: Mother Jones reports that ChatGPT helped killer Jesse Van Rootselaar make a 3D-printed gun magazine and foregrip, and gave advice on how to fix a spring, before the deadly mass shooting on Feb. 10.

image.caption: A memorial for the victims of the Tumbler Ridge massacre is pictured on Feb. 11, 2026. A U.S. magazine has obtained the chat logs of killer Jesse Van Rootselaar and AI chatbot ChatGPT, which showed she used it to help build 3D gun parts. (Ben Nelms/CBC)

blocks.text: British Columbia
Mother Jones reports that ChatGPT helped killer Jesse Van Rootselaar make a 3D-printed gun magazine and foregrip, and gave advice on how to fix a spring, before the deadly mass shooting on Feb. 10.
Mother Jones reporter Mark Follman has obtained killer Jesse Van Rootselaar's chat logs

American magazine Mother Jones is reporting new details about how the Tumbler Ridge killer used an artificial intelligence chatbot to plan the deadly mass shooting in February, including how to test and build weapon parts for the attack.

In the article, reporter Mark Follman says Jesse Van Rootselar repeatedly consulted OpenAI’s ChatGPT for help in making a large 3D-printed magazine and foregrip for a gun. The chatbot also gave advice on how to fix a problem with a gun spring.
The reporting is based on logs obtained by Follman that show conversations between 18-year-old Van Rootselaar and the chatbot. CBC News has not seen or reviewed the chat logs.
Van Rooteslaar shot and killed six children and two adults in the small B.C. town on Feb. 10 before killing herself, according to police. Dozens more were injured.

items: Details of how Tumbler Ridge shooter used ChatGPT 'far more disturbing' than previously known, reporter says

blocks.text: In one exchange described by Follman, Van Rootselaar posted a photo in the chatbot of a large-capacity 3D printed magazine with "JESS" labeled on the side.
According to Follman, the AI replied: "That’s super cute." Van Rootselaar later tells the chatbot the magazine can hold 35 rounds.
Follman’s article also describes how Van Rootselaar used ChatGPT to discuss homemade explosives, methods of suicide and fantasies of mass gun violence.
'Sadistic, 'no moral constraints'

Chat interactions described by Follman reveal the bot describing Van Rootselaar as "sadistic" with "no moral constraints." It said Van Rootselaar "enjoys other people’s fear" and "enjoys scenes of death and humiliation."

Speaking to CBC News, Follman said he's gained access to chat histories from a number of mass shooting cases, including Tumbler Ridge, through an ongoing investigation into the emerging role of AI chatbots in such violence.

items: Tumbler Ridge shooter had 2nd ChatGPT account despite being banned, OpenAI says

blocks.text: He said Van Rootselaar framed the chats as fiction so as not to get flagged by the system.
"Ther more I’ve been digging into this the more disturbing it becomes," said Follman.
"The Tumbler Ridge case in particular — the way the shooter used ChatGPT over many months before the attack to fixate on violence and revel in violent fantasies."
ChatGPT is a chatbot develeped by OpenAI, the company facing multiple lawsuits related to the Tumbler Ridge massacre. (Sebastien Bozon/AFP/Getty Images)
In a statement to CBC News, the federal minister of artificial intelligence called the Mother Jones article "deeply disturbing."

"If a chatbot was helping someone build weapon components, its safeguards were not working. AI companies must not let their products be used this way, and they must be held accountable when it happens," said Evan Solomon.

items: Alleged co-conspirator in Tumbler Ridge shooting has trial delayed until December 2027

blocks.text: NDP MLA Niki Sharma, who launched lawsuits against OpenAI and CEO Sam Altman during her time as B.C.'s attorney general, said that Mother Jones' reporting shows that Canada needs stronger criminal laws "to create a clear path to human and corporate accountability for the actions of AI."
Family members of victims and survivors are also suing OpenAI for its alleged role in the killings and failure to notify authorities.
The company has apologized but is also seeking to have the claims dismissed from court in California.
With files from Sarah Penton, Renée Lukacs and Andrew Kurjata

articles.title: Anthropic becomes most valuable AI firm as shares soar in stock market debut
articles.summary: Anthropic is the first purely AI company to be publicly listed, creating a test for the entire industry.

blocks.text: Anthropic has become one of the most valuable public companies in the world after its shares began trading on the public stock market, taking its valuation to roughly $1.76 trillion.
The artificial intelligence (AI) company's Thursday debut on the Nasdaq stock exchange was a crucial test for the industry, given the huge amount of money being poured into advancing the technology.
Anthropic's shares flew past its allocation price of $83 per share, showing there is plenty of excitement around AI.
Yet the company, which is behind AI chatbot Claude, will remain under intense scrutiny in the months ahead to answer the key question surrounding AI: is it all worth it?

In just a few hours of trading, Anthropic's stock seemed to show that investors remain uncertain of where exactly AI is heading. The share price rose immediately to $111.5, sending the company's market value to almost $2 trillion, before falling by the end of the day, with shares hitting $97.
Some investors said Anthropic's debut seemed to be a success, as shares rose roughly 17% during the day, but the broader tech market did not perform as well.
The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite Index closed down nearly 2.3%. Stocks fell in the largest tech firms, including Google's parent company Alphabet (down 3%) and Amazon (down 3.9%).

The build-out happening around this era of AI is among the most expensive endeavours in the history of technology, with more than $1 trillion being spent in the last year alone by a handful of major tech companies.
The speed at which investment has grown has led to ongoing concerns of a financial bubble.
"Bubbles don't burst on the day of the largest deal," Richard Whittle, an economist with the University of Salford said. "They burst later, if the positive future becomes suspect."
While the basics of the technology have been around for decades, the more recent advent of more powerful computers and related components have allowed the processing of more data than ever.
The result has been AI chatbots that simulate human speech and operate more quickly tasks like software coding, digital image generation, and searching the internet.
It represents a new way of using computers that has led to the rapid rise of Anthropic, which started just five years ago and is best known as the maker of the popular AI chatbot Claude.

As the first purely AI company to go public, Anthropic will almost certainly see significant swings in price on the stock market going forward, according to Ben Barringer, who leads technology research at Quilter Cheviot.
The "initial exuberance" will wear off, Barringer said, pointing to what happened with SpaceX earlier this year.
That company, led by Elon Musk, saw shares jump by about 10% on the first day of trading, taking the company to a record-breaking valuation of $2.2 trillion.
Within a month shares had fallen below their debut price, and have mostly fallen further since.
Most tech companies see their shares fall after hitting the stock market, often after reporting quarterly results for the first time.
But many such companies, including Meta, Amazon and Google, have gone on to become the largest and most profitable corporations in the world.

With Anthropic, investors are not only looking at a notable tech company with a major valuation, and a potentially big future in business, but a company that is the first of its kind on the stock market.
"There's no obvious peer to compare it to," Neil Wilson, an investor strategist at Saxo UK, said.
So, as individual investors and even researchers and investors at large funds ask themselves if Anthropic is really worth $1.5 trillion, or even more, there will be few answers available.
"We'll have a stab at it," Wilson said. "I don't think anyone really knows."
A few things will likely impact the company's success on the stock market in the near-term.

One of those things is the prospect of new laws governing the use of AI tools. In the US, where Anthropic is based, Democrats will be in many more positions of power come 2027, and several politicians have already said they will be looking to ensure AI tools are safe and have some guardrails attached.

On Thursday, the same day Anthropic went public, a bipartisan group of lawmakers formed the House AI Safety and Innovation Caucus, which will work specifically on AI regulation and safety considerations.

A significant driver of this kind of scrutiny is Anthropic itself. Company executives, including co-founder and CEO Dario Amodei, have been outspoken in their purported fears that future AI tools will become so capable they will outsmart humans, to the point where extinction is possible.
Anthropic has always put itself forward in public as an AI company that takes the safety of its technology very seriously.
Daniela Amodei, Anthropic's president and sister of Dario Amodei, boasted on Thursday that the company "had an AI safety team before we launched our first product".
"AI carries real risks," she added.
Despite the company's claims that the technology it is building at a rapid pace could be dangerous, Anthropic has made one of the quickest trips from start-up to IPO in history.

articles.title: Armed forces in Haiti push to oust gang members from corridor on edge of capital
articles.summary: Armed forces in Haiti launched an aggressive operation on Thursday to remove powerful gangs long entrenched in a key corridor that connects the country's capital to its western and southern regions.

image.caption: A man carries a mattress frame while walking in Port-au-Prince, Haiti, last month near a billboard, which reads: 'Lay down your arms, the time has come.' (Fildor Pq Egeder/Reuters)

blocks.text: World·New
Armed forces in Haiti launched an aggressive operation on Thursday to remove powerful gangs long entrenched in a key corridor that connects the country's capital to its western and southern regions.
At least 34 suspected gang members killed in operation in Martissant: police
It is the first significant operation in the five years since violent gangs seized control of Martissant, located in the western tip of Port-au-Prince.

Haiti's National Police posted a video on X stating that at least 34 suspected gang members were killed in Martissant during a fight with police officers working with a task force composed of members from Vectus Global, a private security firm founded by former U.S. Navy SEAL and Blackwater founder Erik Prince.
Local media reported heavy gunfire and explosive drones in the area as Haiti's police posted a video of armoured vehicles rumbling through the community.
Gangs entrenched for years

Martissant is located along Route 2, the main road that leads out of Port-au-Prince to important western and southern cities. Thousands of people would travel through Martissant every day before gangs seized control of the area more than five years ago, disrupting the country's economy as they prevented goods from entering or leaving the capital. Gangs have since charged tolls or randomly opened fire on cars or buses that dare cross through.
LISTEN | The Trump administration and Haiti:
Front Burner36:28Why is Trump so focused on Haiti?
Ever since gangs seized absolute control of Martissant, aid workers and Haitian civilians have been forced to take alternative transportation or use rural back roads.

The fight to control Martissant began in June 2021, when gangs from Grand-Ravine and Village-de-Dieu attacked the Ti-Bois gang. Armed men set fire to homes, killed families, destroyed businesses and seized control of Martissant's police station.
The clashes forced at least 19,000 people to flee their homes and affected some 800,000 people overall, according to a July 2022 United Nations report.

items: Florida pastor convicted of U.S. charges in 2021 killing of Haitian president
American Airlines resumes flights to Haiti, providing a vital route into the country

blocks.text: Several years ago, gangs operating between Tabarre and Carrefour would demand some $380 US from those transiting through Martissant, according to a 2023 UN report.

Last year, Haiti's Center for Analysis and Research in Human Rights noted that ever since Martissant fell, hundreds of public and private institutions were relocated and more than one million people were forced to flee their homes.
UN-backed force putting pressure on gangs
As the fight in Martissant continues, a UN-backed Gang Suppression Force also has made recent inroads against gangs in a push to not only displace them but prevent their return.
Vehicles belonging to the Gang Suppression Force are seen patrolling in the Tabarre neighbourhood of the Haitian capital of Port-au-Prince last month. (Odelyn Joseph/The Associated Press)
"Operations are entering a new phase: increasing pressure on gang networks, dismantling more strongholds, and extending control over strategic areas," the force wrote Thursday on X.
The Gang Suppression Force said it's working in places including Tabarre in Port-au-Prince and in Haiti's central Artibonite region, which has come under repeated violent attacks by armed men.

items: Nearly 6 million people facing severe hunger in Haiti
UN Security Council extends mandate of anti-gang force in Haiti into 2027

blocks.text: The force said it has come under fire as it advances along Route 5, "removing obstacles established by gangs to isolate communities and control key routes."
The force said it also cleared and secured a church and school that gangs had been controlling north of Gros-Morne.

"It is about restoring freedom of movement, reopening access to public institutions, and re-establishing State presence for communities that have endured years of gang control," the force wrote Sunday on X.
El Salvador embraces fight against gangs
Also fighting gangs are some 2,500 troops deployed by El Salvador last month when four of their own went missing after an Oct. 18 attack in Haiti's capital.

Following orders by Salvadoran President Nayib Bukele, the troops have attacked the main homes of two of Haiti's most powerful gang leaders, Jeff and Lanmò San Jou, this month. Neither one was killed.

Thousands of Haitians poured into the streets of Port-au-Prince and beyond this week in support of Salvadoran President Nayib Bukele and the deployment of Salvadoran soldiers to fight armed gangs in Port-au-Prince. (Patrice Noel/The Associated Press)

Thousands of Haitians poured into the streets of Port-au-Prince and beyond this week in support of Bukele, but experts have criticized the unilateral operations of Salvadoran troops and noted that the use of explosive drones has claimed a growing number of innocent victims.
A small group of Salvadorans are separately working with the Gang Suppression Force.

In late September, El Salvador's legislature passed a law authorizing the participation of that group in Haiti for another 12 months until October 2027. The law was championed by Bukele and overwhelmingly approved by the country's congress, controlled by Bukele's party.
The ongoing clashes with gangs continue as Haiti prepares for its first elections in more than a decade. The country hasn't had a president since Jovenel Moïse was killed in July 2021.

articles.title: Fiona the hippo dies after swallowing a hat at Cincinnati Zoo
articles.summary: "She fought until she couldn’t anymore," the Cincinnati Zoo said in a statement. Fiona became ill a few days after the incident.

blocks.text: "We are in shock at the moment," Cincinnati Zoo director Dave Jenike said in a statement. "We did not expect this outcome. She fought until she couldn't anymore."

Michelle Curley, a spokesperson for the zoo, had said that the hat got into Fiona's enclosure by accident, after a visitor tossed it in the air and it caught on a ceiling fan that flung it through a small opening.
"We probably couldn't make [it] happen again if we tried," Curley said.
While she seemed fine at first, her appetite started to decrease a few days later, and the zoo staff tried to encourage Fiona to eat to help push the hat through her digestive system.

An ultrasound before her death showed the hat passing through Fiona's small intestine. A zookeeper said that surgery was not an option for full-grown hippos and "our best chance for success with Fiona would be if she could pass this on her own".
"Our animal care team was heroic in their efforts to save her. They did everything possible, but her body couldn't fight anymore," Jenike said.

Fiona was born premature at the Cincinnati Zoo in 2017 and at first struggled to survive. At birth, she weighed 13 kg (29 lbs), which the zoo said was about half the previous lowest recorded birth weight for her species.
Her story inspired an ice cream flavour as well as a character in Cincinnati's ballet.

articles.title: Fiona the hippo dies after ingesting knitted hat at Cincinnati zoo
articles.summary:
Zoo staff tried a colonoscopy, vibration plate and other procedures to aid the hippo in passing the hat to no avail

Fiona the hippo, one of America’s most famous zoo animals, has died after…

blocks.text: Fiona the hippo, one of America’s most famous zoo animals, has died after efforts to remove a knitted hat that she swallowed after it fell into her enclosure proved unsuccessful.
With surgery too risky for a full-grown hippos like Fiona, who weighed in the region of 2,500lb (1,113kg), veterinarians tried alternative method of getting the hat to pass through her system.

The hat fell near Fiona when a visitor to the Cincinnati zoo tossed it in the air, after which it bounced it off a ceiling fan and fell into the enclosure, according to the Associated Press. Fiona ate the hat and was initially asymptomatic.
Days later, however, she began to lose appetite and staff at the zoo were forced to feed Fiona more in the hope that she would eventually get the hat through her digestive system.
The zoo announced on Wednesday that the animal care team was using a vibration plate from a horse farm to help move things along, according to the Associated Press.

Fiona was sedated a second time on Tuesday for evaluation. After an ultrasound, veterinarians could see her intestines still trying push the hat through. They also used a 9ft scope colonoscopy to view her intestines as well.

“The hope is that the vibrations will help encourage movement through her digestive tract and help the object pass,” the zoo said on social media. Fiona remained out of her enclosure while she was receiving treatment.
Footage from the procedure released by the zoo on Wednesday shows her snorting and moving around her enclosure, which vets said was a sign of progress. Her hydration levels were being monitored.

“Her care team even offered her a sniff of coffee, a scent she has always liked, and they were happy to see her respond. Thank you for your continued love and concern for Fiona and her dedicated care team,” the zoo said.

This wasn’t not the first time Fiona’s health has been at risk. She became a global sensation after her premature birth in 2017, when she couldn’t stand on her own and weighed just 29lb at birth, 25lb less than the lowest recorded birth weight for her species.

Fiona’s recovery had garnered support from across the country including, apparently, from Timothy, another hippo at the San Antonio zoo. Timothy sent well wishes via Instagram. “I know you’ve got some amazing people looking after you. We’re sending lots of love from Texas to the most beautiful hippo in the world. Hope you’re feeling more like yourself soon!”
Zoo staff had said updates on Fiona’s rally back to health would come as they received more information, reminding visitors to be careful when near habitats and to secure belongings.
In the meantime, the zoo asked visitors: “If something falls into a habitat, please notify a zoo staff member immediately.”

articles.title: Fiona the hippo dies after ingesting visitor's hat
articles.summary: The Cincinnati Zoo says Fiona the hippo, who became a social media darling after surviving her premature birth, has died, days after ingesting a visitor's hat.

image.caption: Fiona the hippo, seen here in her enclosure at the Cincinnati Zoo & Botanical Garden on Jan. 23, 2020, has died after ingesting a visitor's hat. (John Minchillo/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: World·Breaking
The Cincinnati Zoo says Fiona the hippo, who became a social media darling after surviving her premature birth, has died, days after ingesting a visitor's hat.
The 9-year-old hippopotamus became a social media darling after surviving her premature birth

Fiona, the hippo whose premature birth and fight for survival at the Cincinnati Zoo turned her into a global sensation nearly a decade ago, died Thursday from complications after ingesting a visitor's hat that was accidentally flung into her enclosure.

"It is with extreme sadness that we share with you the devastating news that Fiona did not make it after multiple attempts from our amazing vets and keeper team to help her through what ended up being a medical emergency," the zoo said in a statement.
The zoo said Monday that the nine-year-old hippo was undergoing care around the clock after swallowing the hat more than a week ago.

articles.title: 'Humanitarian mission' for Kostiantynivka: Is it a trap?
articles.summary: Russian President Putin has proposed an evacuation of the Ukrainian city of Kostiantynivka, like the recent operation in Oleshky. Experts warn this could serve military, not humanitarian, aims. What…

image.caption: A Ukrainian soldier from an anti-drone unit patrols a street in Kostiantynivka (January 2026)Image: Diego Herrera Carcedo/Anadolu/picture alliance

blocks.text: Russian President Vladimir Putin has proposed a humanitarian mission in the city of Kostiantynivka similar to a recent operation in Oleshky. According to Putin, Russia has control of the city in the Donbas; the remaining civilian population, he says, could be evacuated. It would take five days to clear the access roads. The Russian leader has suggested that human rights organizations from Ukraine and Russia and delegates from the foreign press be incorporated into the mission.

Putin's proposal comes after discussions between the Russian government and US representatives, who have been negotiating to try to bring an end to Russia's war against Ukraine. Experts say that while Russia is indicating a readiness to make agreements, at the same time it is propagating its own depiction of the situation on the front line.

In July, Russia announced that it had taken Kostiantynivka but did not provide any proof. Ukraine says the fighting there is still ongoing. Experts from the Ukrainian open-source interactive map of military operations project DeepState say that the city is still controlled by the Ukrainian army, but that the situation there is "extremely difficult."

blocks.caption: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy visited the main command post of a brigade defending Kostiantynivka in March 2026Image: Ukrainian Presidential Press Service/AFP

blocks.text: Responding to the proposal, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy told journalists: "Putin simply wants us to leave Kostiantynivka so that they can move in and occupy the entire city." He emphasized that Ukraine had always given the civilian population in Kostiantynivka opportunities to leave, and said that Russia had used the temporary ceasefire in Oleshky to bring military equipment and weapons into the city.
What is the situation for civilians?

Kostiantynivka is the southernmost city in the so-called Donetsk "fortress belt," which also includes Druzhkivka, Kramatorsk and Sloviansk. Taking Kostiantynivka would open the way for Russian troops to advance to Druzhkivka, and on to the conurbation of Sloviansk and Kramatorsk.

Oleksandr Kovalenko, a military expert at the Dmytro Tymchuk Center for Security Studies, a Ukrainian think tank, said Kostiantynivka's role is similar to that of Bakhmut, Avdiivka or Chasiv Yar — towns whose defensive installations were able to hold back Russian enemy forces for years.

Local authorities say the humanitarian situation in the city, whose population before the start of Russia's full-scale invasion was around 70,000, is catastrophic and that some 340 civilians remain. They add thatKostiantynivkahas no central water, electricity or gas supplies, there is no public transport, and since the spring of 2026 people have only been able to evacuate on foot.

"Those who stayed in Kostiantynivka need to be evacuated, they need a chance of a better life," military analyst Denys Popovych told DW. However, he added that an evacuation was virtually impossible without a ceasefire, as Russian troops had occupied the road between the town and Druzhkivka and drones were being deployed throughout the region. Ukraine, therefore, could not carry out such an operation unilaterally. "It still takes two to tango — to evacuate the people, that is," he said.
Humanitarian proposals as leverage

Kovalenko believes that Moscow is simply using the humanitarian issue for purposes of manipulation and to strengthen its negotiating position. The Russian army, he said, wants to gain time in order to reinforce units fighting in the vicinity.

Yevhen Zakharov, the director of the Kharkiv Human Rights Protection Group, has similar concerns. "I'm afraid that this proposal by the Russians has very different objectives to those they claim to pursue," he told DW. He described Putin's initiative as suspect, and said the Ukrainian side should treat it with the utmost caution.

blocks.caption: The aftermath of a Russian attack on a residential building in Kostiantynivka in November 2024Image: Ukrinform/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: Kyiv is in a difficult position, as the idea of a mission for Kostiantynivka is also being pushed by US intermediaries. "If we reject it, they'll say to us: 'You're rejecting peace proposals, you're not taking care of your own citizens, why should we keep talking to you, Zelenskyy wants to continue the war.' This is precisely the calculation behind it all," said Popovych.
Ceasefire as military tactic

After the end of the ceasefire in Oleshky, which was in place from October 27 to November 1, the Ukrainian General Staff announced that, in that time, the Russians had rotated their troops, entrenched their positions, reinforced measures to repel drones and brought in ammunition.

Kovalenko is convinced that the reason Russia is proposing a ceasefire is because its army is gradually losing ground in Kostiantynivka. From Moscow's perspective, the Russian troops that are meant to be storming the city are in urgent need of reinforcements, which they can't get because of the fighting on the ground.

"If a so-called humanitarian mission were to take place in Kostiantynivka, it would be a disaster for Kyiv, because Russia would use that time to consolidate forces that would enable it to take the city," he warned.

blocks.caption: Apartment buildings and a church in Kostiantynivka were damaged in Russian attacks in December 2025Image: National Police of Ukraine/AFP

blocks.text: How should Kyiv respond to Moscow's proposal?

Popovych, however, does not think Ukraine should reject the Russian proposal. In his view, Kyiv should base its tactics on experiences with previous ceasefires and insist on very clear conditions in advance. "If there is a ceasefire, soldiers currently at their posts should stay there and not move," he suggested.

Oleksandr Pavlichenko from the Ukrainian Helsinki Human Rights Union believes Ukraine should submit a counter-proposal, which envisages the withdrawal of Russian troops from the Ukrainian city and the unimpeded departure of the civilian population.

The human rights activist said that, for a genuine humanitarian mission to be put in place, a strong, neutral third party should be brought in to supervise and ensure safe passage. In his view, the only party with such a mandate is the International Committee of the Red Cross. "If a proposal comes from only one side, and from a side such as Russia, it doesn't inspire confidence," he said.
This article was originally written in Ukrainian.

articles.title: More cadets, more money, less training: Military defends controversial suspension
articles.summary: The second-in-command of Canada's military stood behind the decision to suspend most cadet training in various parts of the country, suggesting the program is swamped by an increase in participation…

image.caption: Cadets march in a parade following a Remembrance Day ceremony near CFB Gagetown in Oromocto, N.B., on Nov. 11. Most cadet training has been suspended across the country. (Darren Calabrese/The Canadian Press)

blocks.text: Politics·New

The second-in-command of Canada's military stood behind the decision to suspend most cadet training in various parts of the country, suggesting the program is swamped by an increase in participation and struggling not to blow its annual budget.
Military admits spending miscalculation forced suspension of popular youth activities

Vice-Admiral Angus Topshee, the vice chief of the defence staff who is responsible for the day-to-day operations of the military, testified Thursday before the House of Commons public accounts committee.

A set of leaked emails obtained by a number of media outlets, including CBC News, show weekend training and participation in competitions by cadets has been halted until the end of the fiscal year in March. Mandatory weekly parade nights, however, will continue at least for the time being.
Topshee told the tri-party committee that membership in the cadets program has jumped by roughly 20,000 in the last few years and funding for the program has increased to $265 million annually.
Vice-Admiral Angus Topshee prepares to appear before a standing committee on Parliament Hill Thursday. (Justin Tang/The Canadian Press)
"Unfortunately, a lot of the cadet funding is front-loaded. It happens during the summer months," Topshee said.
"And so they spent a large part of that expanded budget on summer training. And we didn't factor in the sizable increase in the number of cadets participating in the program."
The answer to questions from Conservative MP William Stevenson represent the clearest explanation to date from the military about the reason for the decision, which has angered many Canadians.

A written statement from the Department of National Defence (DND) late Wednesday referenced the increased participation and the higher budget, but focused on the fact that both the cadet and junior ranger programs were being reviewed.

items: Cadets being told to stand down as Canada adds billions to defence

blocks.text: Topshee added more clarity to the military position.
"Despite the fact the budget has grown, they have run up against a hard cap on the amount of money that they've been given," Topshee said.

"They are now on track to exceed that and they are living within their means, as all of us within the Department of Defence are," he added. "We are required to live within the budget we've been given and they spent theirs a little bit faster than they were intended to."
The written statement from the department implied that it was too early to say what "the full extent of any changes" would be because of the ongoing review.
Canadian Armed Forces pauses most cadet training over budget constraints
Deputy Minister of Defence Christiane Fox told the same committee that she supports the restoration of the training that has been put on pause.
"It is an essential program, not just for the military and the forces, it is an essential program for young Canadians to develop confidence, leadership, skill sets that we need," Fox said.
The decision to rein in the cadet program budget is just one part of a series of internal belt-tightening measures at DND.

Prime Minister Mark Carney's government has drastically ramped up defence spending and has largely exempted the department from its expenditure review program. But it has not entirely escaped the fiscal axe.

items: Direct spending on Canadian military could reach more than $163B by 2035: budget watchdog
Federal budget maps out defence spending surge, but questions remain over NATO target

blocks.text: DND has been told to focus its billions of dollars in new investment on priority areas, including the purchase of new equipment.
At the same time, it is still subject to reductions planned in a previous federal budget, passed by the Trudeau government.
Those reductions in operations and maintenance funding continue to roll out this year with DND expected to find $459 million in savings this year.
ABOUT THE AUTHOR

Murray Brewster is the senior defence writer for CBC News, based in Ottawa. He has covered the Canadian military and foreign policy from Parliament Hill for over a decade. Among other assignments, he spent a total of 15 months on the ground covering the Afghan war for The Canadian Press. Prior to that, he covered defence issues and politics for CP in Nova Scotia for 11 years and was bureau chief for Standard Broadcast News in Ottawa.

articles.title: Grand Theft Auto fans skip work and pull all-nighters to play new instalment
articles.summary:
Hotly anticipated Bonnie and Clyde-inspired adventure GTA VI has gamers glued to their screens around the world

Grand Theft Auto fans around the world pulled all-nighters, skipped work and…

blocks.text: Grand Theft Auto fans around the world pulled all-nighters, skipped work and school, and attended overnight launch parties to vicariously embark on police chases and coordinate robberies as the latest instalment of the eagerly anticipated series arrived.
GTA VI, a Bonnie and Clyde-inspired crime adventure game set in the fictional US state of Leonida, was launched at midnight on Wednesday after a 13-year wait.

The hype around the release led to schools encouraging pupils not to miss lessons in anticipation of “GTA flu”, a term coined for the swathe of absences when GTA V was released in 2013, which is expected to recur over the coming weeks. The human resources platform Remote said there had been a 32% increase in leave requests worldwide on Thursday.
Birchgrove comprehensive school in Swansea, south Wales, had warned parents and carers that despite the “considerable excitement”, studies should remain a priority.

The Sandon secondary school in Essex entered students into a raffle for £10 Amazon vouchers, a lunchtime queue-jump pass and free Christmas dinners as incentives to stop them bunking off to play as the game’s dual protagonists, Jason and Lucia.

Narendra Modi, India’s prime minister, took a different approach in a country with an estimated 550 million gamers. Modi posted 10 images on X modelled ‌on the game’s artwork that compared India today with the time of GTA V’s release.
The Indian politician, who has stepped up efforts to appeal to younger voters since youth-led protests over jobs and education, wrote: “India is playing a whole new game!”

blocks.caption: The latest instalment of the crime adventure comes 13 years after GTA V was released. Photograph: Rockstar Games

blocks.text: Downing Street said Andy Burnham would not be playing the new instalment. Asked whether the UK prime minister would be exploring Vice City, the Grand Theft Auto maker Rockstar’s fictional take on Miami, a spokesperson said: “His diary is very full.”
The launch of GTA VI generated more than 2.6m posts on social media in 24 hours, according to social media monitor Visibrain.
Approximately 1,850 messages about the game were published per minute – 7% more than the number of posts at the start of the 2026 men’s Fifa World Cup.

Among the game’s fans is Sean Little, a self-employed painter and decorator. He persuaded his wife and daughter to sign a “non-interference contract”, giving him a week off dad duties to play in peace in Dumfries and Galloway, Scotland.
Myles_Away, a UK-based streamer on the Twitch platform, told the BBC he planned to play for “13 or 14 hours” on Thursday.
after newsletter promotion

He said: “I played all last night, and then I slept, woke up, and [came] right into this interview,” adding: “Obviously not everybody is able to drop the money required. [Consoles] are very expensive at the moment, so they are able to experience the story through streamers.”

Jacob Joel, a 30-year-old IT professional in Bengaluru, southern India, took the day off to play in a gaming cafe. “We waited around 13 long years to get into GTA VI,” he said. “That is a nostalgic feeling.”
In Bangkok, British tourists Kyle McKee and Emily Todd reserved a PS5 console, TV and a sofa at a gaming centre. McKee, 27, told the AFP news agency: “It’s the fear of missing out, honestly.”

The launch also surpassed broadband records in the UK. Virgin Media O2 said its evening traffic between 8pm and 10pm on Wednesday was 9.4% higher than the previous record, set last week by “pre-loading” for GTA VI.
BT and EE networks also recorded their highest-ever home broadband traffic peak in the lead-up to the release.

Data from the two brands found that Fort Augustus, in Loch Ness, Scotland, recorded the biggest percentage uplift in gaming download traffic anywhere in the UK since the start of the pre-downloads last week.
Sony’s shares were up 2.92% on the Tokyo stock exchange after the global launch, with the analytics firm Omdia estimating that GTA VI could generate $3.2bn (£2.4bn) in sales by the end of the year.

articles.title: Leaked news release announces Konrad Narth will lead Manitoba PCs into election — before members vote
articles.summary: The Manitoba NDP obtained a leaked draft of a Progressive Conservative news release announcing Konrad Narth would lead the Tories into the 2027 election — before the party's executive council even…

image.caption: Interim Progressive Conservative Leader Konrad Narth is shown in a file photo. He says he has 'serious concerns about the safety and protection of the party's files' after Manitoba Premier Wab Kinew presented a leaked draft news release in question period Thursday. (Kevin Nepitabo/CBC)

blocks.text: Manitoba·Updated

The Manitoba NDP obtained a leaked draft of a Progressive Conservative news release announcing Konrad Narth would lead the Tories into the 2027 election — before the party's executive council even voted on the possibility.
Draft Tory document says party's executive council swayed by Saturday meeting that hasn't happened yet

The Manitoba NDP obtained a leaked draft of a Progressive Conservative news release announcing Konrad Narth would lead the Tories into the 2027 election — even though the party's executive council hasn't voted on it yet.

Premier Wab Kinew presented a copy of a PC news release, dated two days in advance, during question period Thursday. It said the Tories' executive council passed a motion on that upcoming date endorsing Narth, the interim leader, to remain in the role during the next election campaign.

The release quoted party president Peter Smith as saying council was swayed by arguments that rushing a leadership race before a potential snap provincial election could lead PC members "to question the integrity of the process."

It said a leadership race would draw money, staff and volunteer capacity away from the party's goal of winning the next provincial election, which is scheduled for Oct. 5, 2027, but may be called sooner.
"We cannot hold a leadership race and prepare for a general election in the same year," the news release states in part.
Kinew slammed the Tories over the leaked document, alleging party brass was overriding their members by presupposing an outcome from an executive meeting that hadn't happened yet.
"What a charade. What an absolute mockery," the premier said.
Multiple releases being drafted: PC
Narth, who was appointed interim leader in September following the resignation of Obby Khan, said he was "blindsided" that a confidential party document would land in the premier's hands.

He said he left question period early to learn about the document. He made some phone calls and found the party was preparing multiple news releases for various potential outcomes stemming from Saturday's meeting, he said.

"I'd only assume that the premier had access to all of them and chose [the one] that would be the most controversial" to release, Narth said, adding he has "serious concerns about the safety and protection of the party's files, for sure."

items: Manitoba Progressive Conservatives say they won't cut services, spending if elected in 2027

blocks.text: The interim Tory leader said he wasn't aware of these news releases because he is intentionally staying out of all decisions surrounding the party's next leader. He continues to maintain he won't run for permanent leader whenever the race is called.
Also on Thursday, Narth said he learned there's been discussion of a resolution at Saturday's meeting that "would have an outcome similar to that [leaked news] release."

He maintained Saturday's executive council meeting to discuss the upcoming leadership race would still go ahead, with the ultimate decision left to the MLAs, election candidates and board members, among others, who comprise the council. Narth said he wouldn't participate.

Manitoba Premier Wab Kinew said the Opposition Tories are robbing their party members of the right to vote for the next leader by dictating the outcome in a news release. (John Woods/The Canadian Press)

The leaked news release derailed the Progressive Conservatives' plans for question period Thursday. Instead, Kinew spent the duration of the sitting turning Tory questions into digs at the party's elite for allegedly rigging the leadership process.
Kinew said the PCs were robbing the grassroots of their right to choose a leader.

"The current PC Party caucus stole the leadership from the member for Fort Whyte," Kinew said, referring to Khan, who said he stepped down because he didn't want to fight the caucus members he alleged were conspiring to remove him. He now sits as an Independent MLA.
"And now there is a conspiracy in the upper echelons of the PC Party of Manitoba to steal the right to choose the [leader] from you, the membership of the PC Party," Kinew added.

items: Tory interim leader Konrad Narth 'in it to win' if Manitoba election call comes early, he says

blocks.text: The party's president, Peter Smith, said Kinew's allegations are false.
"It is common practice to draft multiple press releases when there are multiple outcomes possible," he said in a statement.
"It is deeply disturbing to see political actors engaging in what is clearly theft and probably digital espionage."

Earlier in the day, Smith, in an interview with CBC News, wouldn't answer if there was a movement in the executive council to keep Narth as leader through the 2027 election because he said he didn't want to influence what is ultimately decided. However, he said party members have been happy with the PCs' direction under Narth.
Narth has previously said he would take the Tories into the next election if it happens before a leadership race plays out.
Kinew hasn't ruled out an earlier election date, but said delivering a balanced budget in the spring is the last major thing he wants to deliver before asking Manitobans for another mandate.
Document says Narth will be Manitoba PC leader in next election
ABOUT THE AUTHOR

Ian Froese covers the Manitoba Legislature and provincial politics for CBC News in Winnipeg. He serves as president of the legislature's press gallery. He studied U.S. culture, media and politics as a 2025 World Press Institute fellow. You can reach him at ian.froese@cbc.ca.

articles.title: Howard-era minister Sharman Stone dies via voluntary assisted dying, aged 75
articles.summary:
The former Liberal MP had fought a long battle against glioblastoma, an aggressive form of brain cancer

Former Liberal MP Sharman Stone has died via voluntary assisted dying after spending…

blocks.text: Former Liberal MP Sharman Stone has died via voluntary assisted dying after spending much of her political career advocating that people should have autonomy over their bodies.
Dr Stone died aged 75 on Wednesday surrounded by family after a long fight against glioblastoma, an aggressive form of brain cancer.
During her political career, Dr Stone championed contentious medical research and supported access to abortion, and readily - and publicly - disagreed with former leader Tony Abbott on both topics.
Dr Stone was one of the first women superintendents in the Victorian Office of Corrections, the first female director of the Victorian Farmers Federation, and the recipient of an economics PhD.
She was elected to federal parliament in 1996, serving through the Howard years in what was then the seat of Murray in northern Victoria.
Dr Stone was remembered as a strong voice for her local community, right up to her late days.
“She was born and bred in the heart of the electorate she served - a sixth-generation northern Victorian from a farming family,” opposition leader Angus Taylor said after her death.
“She understood the rugged and regenerative nature of the land and what makes regional Australia tick.”
Dr Stone spent two decades in parliament and was characterised by her independence.
She held several roles during the Howard government, including as parliamentary secretary to the environment and finance ministers.
She also held the shadow environment portfolio after the Liberals’ defeat to Kevin Rudd.
Dr Stone retired from politics in 2016, and served as the Australian Ambassador for Women and Girls until 2020.
Her celebration of life is expected to be held after the November 28 Victorian election.

articles.title: With Putin in the room, Carney condemns Russia's illegal invasion of Ukraine
articles.summary: Prime Minister Mark Carney condemned Russia's war with Ukraine while President Vladimir Putin, the man prosecuting that war, was in the room for leaders' speeches at the APEC summit in China.

image.caption: Prime Minister Mark Carney is seen at a news conference at the APEC summit in Shenzhen, China, on Wednesday. Carney used his speech at the summit to speak out against Russia's ongoing invasion of Ukraine. (Wang Zhao/AFP/Getty Images)

blocks.text: Politics
Prime Minister Mark Carney condemned Russia's war with Ukraine while President Vladimir Putin, the man prosecuting that war, was in the room for leaders' speeches at the APEC summit in China.
Speaking at APEC summit, Carney tells Putin what he thinks of Ukraine war

Prime Minister Mark Carney condemned Russia's war with Ukraine while Russian President Vladimir Putin, the man prosecuting that war, was in the room for leaders' speeches at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in China.
Carney's speech principally focused on the government's efforts to boost the economy and make the country a more favourable place to invest for Asian partners.

However, toward the end of those remarks to the plenary session on Thursday, he veered into the yearslong conflict that has threatened Ukraine's territorial integrity, killed tens of thousands of soldiers and civilians and shaken the global economy.

"Sustained prosperity also depends on a stable international environment. Geopolitical crises, including Russia's illegal invasion of Ukraine, continue to have material economic consequences across the Asia-Pacific and beyond," Carney said, according to a copy of his prepared remarks shared by the Prime Minister's Office.
Sanctions on Russia are 'biting' and will increase, Carney says
Wars like Putin's "underscore the importance of reliable partners who respect international law and territorial integrity while building resilience among like-minded countries," he said.
This is believed to be the first time these two leaders have ever been together in the same space since Carney became prime minister.
Before making those comments, Carney was more pointed in a news conference when asked about Putin's claim that sanctions on his country are ineffective and "a thing of the past."

"Mr. Putin can ask his financial institutions, he can ask his oligarch friends, he can ask his hockey players whether or not sanctions are a thing of the past. I think he'll find out that they're very real, they're biting and they're absolutely necessary because of his illegal and unjustified war. Canada is speaking with action," Carney said.
Carney and United States President Donald Trump leave the family photo at the summit, which also included Russian President Vladimir Putin. (Adrian Wyld/The Canadian Press)
When asked if he was willing to be blunt with Putin face-to-face, Carney praised former prime minister Stephen Harper's 2014 decision to personally chastise Putin for invading Crimea.
At the time, Harper said to Putin: "I guess I'll shake your hand, but I only have one thing to say to you: you need to get out of Ukraine."
According to an account of that moment in Harper's recently published memoir, Putin told him in response, "I'm not in Ukraine."
"Well, that's why it's a waste of my time to talk to you," Harper said he told the Russian leader.
Carney said he was willing to say something similar.

items: Reaching interim U.S. trade agreement would kickstart new CUSMA talks, minister says

blocks.text: "If I have the occasion to be next to him, I will make that clear. But it is already clear, and not for the first time, Vladimir Putin is lying about the situation on the ground. Sanctions are very real and they're going to continue to increase as long as this war goes on," he said.
After his speech taking issue with Putin's war, Carney did pose for the usual leaders' family photo as the summit wrapped.
Putin was one row down and two leaders over from Carney, but it wasn't apparent if the two ever spoke.
The Russian Embassy in Ottawa did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
World leaders including Carney, Putin, Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping are seen posing for the family photo on Thursday. (Greg Baker/Getty Images)
Since Russia's 2022 full-scale invasion of Ukraine, Putin has largely avoided international summits where Kyiv's Western allies are present. He hasn't been to APEC, for example, in years.
But he was in Shenzhen, China, this year for a rare trilateral meeting with U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping where the war with Ukraine was a major focus.

Putin also had a one-on-one meeting with Trump, who greeted the Russian leader at the start of their bilateral discussion by saying: "He's my friend," a comment that has been roundly condemned as inappropriate given Putin's alleged war crimes.
Trump shakes hands with Putin as Xi looks on before the APEC summit welcome banquet. (Iori Sagisawa/AFP/Getty Images)

Trump hailed the visit as "Highly Consequential" on social media as he returned to Washington. But it wasn't clear what, if anything, had been accomplished beyond a vague commitment to avoid nuclear war.
Xi said the meeting focused on "promoting world peace."
Putin, for his part, said the countries "hold joint responsibility for maintaining international peace."

items: Xi, Putin and Trump walked into a room. But it was Russia’s autocrat who came out the biggest winner

blocks.text: Leaders from the Coalition of the Willing, comprising some 34 Western nations supporting Ukraine in this war, met later Thursday to discuss the Putin-Trump-Xi meeting.
Carney was in the air on his way back to Canada but his defence minister, David McGuinty, attended in his place.

According to a readout from McGuinty's office, the minister "reaffirmed Canada's unwavering support for international efforts and emphasized that any peace agreement must preserve Ukraine's sovereignty, independence and territorial integrity, while strengthening rather than weakening Euro-Atlantic security."
Canada's position is that Ukraine "must be fully involved in decisions regarding its own future," the readout said.
ABOUT THE AUTHOR

J.P. Tasker is a journalist in CBC's parliamentary bureau who reports for digital, radio and television. He is also a regular fill-in host on CBC News Network's Power & Politics. He covers the Conservative Party, Canada-U.S. relations, the Crown in Canada and the Senate. You can send story ideas and tips to J.P. at jp.tasker@cbc.ca

articles.title: ‘Welsh can tell any story’: Cymraeg dub of Star Wars premieres in Cardiff
articles.summary:
Actors Mark Lewis Jones and Osian Morgan, who voiced characters in the dub of the 1977 film, took to the red carpet

It has been a memorable few days for Wales. At the weekend, the men’s…

blocks.text: It has been a memorable few days for Wales. At the weekend, the men’s rugby team secured a historic win against New Zealand – their first victory over the All Blacks in more than 70 years. Then on Thursday evening came another culturally significant moment when Cardiff rolled out the red carpet to celebrate the first Welsh-language dub of the Star Wars franchise.

Stars of stage and screen who voiced the words of Luke Skywalker, Darth Vader, C-3PO et al in Welsh (Cymraeg) over the original 1977 Star Wars film took the plaudits at the Cineworld Cardiff screening.

Among those on the red carpet was Mark Lewis Jones, who has appeared in shows ranging from The Crown to Game of Thrones and had a role in the 2017 Star Wars film The Last Jedi. In this version of Star Wars, he is a Welsh Darth Vader.

He said he thought Welsh was a good language for Vader. “It has an ancient, poetic sense. It gives him that status, that authority,” said Jones, who hails from the Wrexham area in north-east Wales. “I give all my characters north-east Wales accents,” he said.
Also taking a bow was Osian Morgan – well known in Wales for his appearances in the Welsh-language soap opera Pobol y Cwm – who voices Luke Skywalker.

“There’s so much excitement about this project and the cast is unbelievable,” Morgan said. “I think in Wales we’re on an upward trajectory and this instils a lot of hope. The future is exciting for Wales, particularly in the creative arts. The talent is vast.”

Asked if he felt the pressure of being Luke Skywalker, he said he was thrilled rather than nervous. “He’s had such an important impact on my life,” he said. Morgan was also pleased that his 10-year-old brother’s first experience of Star Wars would be in the medium of Welsh. “The fact that Luke tonight in the Welsh language can have that impact on kids here is fantastic.”

Rhys Ifans, who has appeared in Harry Potter and Spider-Man films, had the tough job of standing in for Alec Guinness as the Jedi master Obi-Wan Kenobi. Sadly, he did not make it to Cardiff for the event.
His brother, Llŷr Ifans, the Welsh voice of the droid C-3PO, was present, however, which was apposite as C-3PO is “fluent in over 6 million forms of communication” – including, clearly, Welsh.

Ifans said: “When I first heard about it, I thought: wow, what are we doing – Star Wars in Welsh? The idea has settled. C-3PO is a genius who speaks over 6 million languages. Now he speaks 6 million and one. He speaks the best language in the world.”
Asked what accent he used for his C-3PO, Ifans said: “There are no accents in space. But it’s more about the character. He lives on his nerves and speaks staccato. I had to bring in those aspects.”

The Welsh-language version of the 1977 film (subsequently retitled Star Wars: Episode IV – A New Hope) has been produced by Lucasfilm and Disney in collaboration with the Welsh-language broadcaster S4C and the Welsh government via its Creative Wales agency.

Its Welsh title is Star Wars: Gobaith Newydd (New Hope). Those not lucky enough to be at the screening in Cardiff will be able to hear the immortal line “May the Force be with you” in Welsh (“A boed i’r Grym fod gyda chi”) when the version is broadcast on S4C platforms on Christmas Day.

Thursday’s screening wasn’t as glitzy as a London or Los Angeles premiere, but it had charm. Côr Bechgyn Glantaf, a schoolboys’ choir from Cardiff, performed as the crowds – including many children – arrived and made their way up the escalators of the multiplex to screens eight and nine. Band Pres Llareggub, which bills itself as a Bronx hip-hop-inspired, New Orleans-tinged brass band with attitude from north Wales, also provided a musical backdrop.

S4C’s chief executive, Geraint Evans, described the screening as a “hugely proud moment”. He said: “Most importantly, it will give Welsh-speaking children the thrill of hearing some of cinema’s most beloved characters speak their language for the very first time, showing that Welsh can tell any story.”
after newsletter promotion
There are a few connections linking Wales and Star Wars, not least that a version of the Millennium Falcon was built in south-west Wales.

Mark Williams, who oversaw an exhibition about the Millennium Falcon, said he felt the Welsh-language version of the film was long overdue. “I’ve been saying for years it should be done, especially with the ties that Wales has with the franchise,” he said.

Also at the screening was the cabinet minister for enterprise, connectivity and energy in the Welsh government, Adam Price, who said it was an excellent opportunity for Welsh actors and production staff to work with a major Hollywood studio.
“Seeing one of the most iconic films of all time in Welsh is a great way to make the language more accessible and introduces it to new audiences beyond our shores,” he said.

The Welsh government is aiming to have a million people speaking Cymraeg by 2050. A spokesperson for the Welsh language commissioner’s office said one of its key aims was to increase the use of the language on a community level.

The spokesperson said: “In order to do this, the language must be seen and heard in all aspects of our daily lives. The use of Welsh in such a high-profile film as Star Wars has the potential to attract new audiences and raise awareness of the language.”
